sources.title: Secretary Kissinger’s Visit to Peking: Counterpart Discussions on Exchanges and Claims/Assets (Second Session)
sources.source_type: Contemporaneous State Department memorandum reconstructed from participant notes; official archival scan

reading_scope.read: Printed 1–11 / physical 35–45 of 46-page folder scan, complete morning meeting including exchanges and claims; archival cover also read. Other folder records not systematically read.
reading_scope.visual_checks: Physical 35 and 40–45: header and complete claims section, printed 6–11.

findings.finding: Record says the secretary mislaid the stenographic pad after returning to Washington; memorandum is based on Armstrong’s notes.

Habib says he reviewed the record and excluded bonds from the settlement; Lin objects that non-espousal leaves private claims possible. Habib corrects the assertion that he said the US had never raised the issue.
Habib seeks definitions protecting against asset owners’ suits; Lin objects to the political implications of 1950 categories and says the December 22 aide-mémoire changed method, not substance.
Habib wants all items within the package; Lin invokes third-country/bank relationships and says a political package need not include every small item. Discussion ends inconclusively.

limits: Official contemporary reconstruction, not a verbatim transcript.
American recording of attributed Chinese positions; no Chinese parallel record or internal instruction.
Lin’s accounts of the December instrument, banks’ interventions, expected reaction and reasons for withdrawal are assertions made in negotiation, not independently established causes.
sources.archive: Ford Library, National Security Adviser, Kissinger Reports on USSR, China, and Middle East Discussions, Box 2, November 25–29, 1974—Kissinger’s Trip (3)
sources.source_independence: A distinct contemporary US record of the next session after CLA-F01; the same officials and dispute do not constitute independent confirmation of their assertions.

sources.title: Memorandum of conversation, Beijing, November 28, 1974, 4:00–6:15 p.m.; FRUS 1969–1976 XVIII, document 98
sources.source_type: Official edited publication of a contemporary US meeting record

reading_scope.depth: Selected substantive passage; all editorial notes
reading_scope.read: Complete claims/assets exchange, printed 628–629, from Kissinger’s reference to Habib’s conversations through the transition to exchanges; immediate context, header and all eight editorial/source notes. Some surrounding passages read, but no claim to complete reading of the long meeting.
reading_scope.visual_checks: HTML text; no underlying scan inspection in this pass.

findings.finding: Kissinger promises to seek wording compatible with Chinese principles and accepts the principle that American law does not apply to China; he does not supply a finished definition.
Identifies Ford Box 2 meeting provenance and the morning November 28 counterpart discussion.

limits: A promise to work on wording and acceptance of a principle are not a completed settlement.
No inference that the statement resolved the underlying legal problem or reveals Chinese private motives.

sources.source_independence: Senior meeting following Habib’s briefing, not an independent adjudication of the counterpart dispute.

sources.title: Department of State briefing paper: Claims/Assets
sources.source_type: Contemporaneous internal State briefing paper preserved in official Ford archival scan

reading_scope.depth: Complete four-page target paper; selected folder
reading_scope.read: Physical 3–6 / printed 1–4 of 32-page folder, all Claims/Assets paper; cover metadata inspected. Other papers not systematically read.

findings.finding: Recommends Ford not raise the question; even unexpected Chinese acceptance should not be formalized before consultation with key members of Congress.
Recounts June 1974 withdrawal; explicitly labels its explanations speculative and lists normalization, domestic rivalries, low priority, MFN linkage and other-country precedent.
Treats claimant and congressional acceptability as constraints; attributes possible motives to China and describes political/commercial advantages of settlement. Date is November 1975, without day.

limits: Recommendation to the President, not proof that he approved or carried it out.
Judgments about Chinese unwillingness, a pretext and competing motives are internal American interpretations.
No congressional vote on the China proposal independently acquired here; no new claim about constitutional requirements.
sources.archive: Ford Library, National Security Adviser Trip Briefing Books and Cables for President Ford, 1974–1976, Box 18, November 28–December 7, 1975—Far East—Briefing Book—Briefing Book—Peking—Bilateral Issues—Scowcroft’s Copy (2)
sources.source_independence: Related State retrospective assessment drawing on the ongoing official record, not independent Chinese corroboration.

sources.title: State 105075: US–PRC claims negotiations
sources.source_type: Public reproduction of a released State Department electronic cable; non-government host

reading_scope.read: Entire header, all four numbered paragraphs, signature, reproduced raw content and metadata. Two cable pages; surrounding website boilerplate is not research evidence.
reading_scope.visual_checks: HTML text; linked raw PDF returned 404, so no scan comparison.

findings.finding: Quotes March 21, 1973 statement excluding old bonds, asserting a general successor-obligation principle without addressing it then, promising non-espousal and leaving direct negotiation to bondholders or representatives and governments concerned.
Says copies of Paris telegraphic exchanges and the draft are being pouched; those enclosures are not included here.
Reports Ni Yao-li’s May 4 explanation to Freeman that the new bond subject required Chinese study.
Recommends low-key opportunistic inquiry instead of seeking a special meeting; drafted by C. W. Freeman Jr.; Rush signature.

limits: Mirror metadata, not an official-host acquisition; no underlying scan verified.
Quotation of the March statement is not the complete original enclosure or successive drafts.
Does not establish that the December 22 memorandum broke an assurance or that the exclusion demanded acknowledgment of all old liabilities.
sources.release_status: Mirror labels current classification UNCLASSIFIED; disposition RELEASED; State systematic-review marking 30 JUN 2005. Historical SECRET/EXDIS markings remain in reproduced text.
sources.source_independence: Contemporaneous US cable supplying an earlier statement and reported conversation; mirror and later advocacy quotation are not separate sources.

sources.title: State 248454: US/PRC claims negotiations, repeating State 209591 of October 24, 1973
sources.source_type: Public reproduction of a released State cable retransmitting a 1973 instruction; non-government host

reading_scope.read: Entire outer header and retransmission, all reproduced October 24, 1973 paragraphs, both signatures and metadata. Rendered content has four PAGE labels although metadata says Page Count 3.
reading_scope.visual_checks: HTML text; no official-host or scan comparison.

findings.finding: October 18, 1975 cable signed Ingersoll explicitly repeats October 24, 1973 State 209591 signed Kissinger; not a newly composed 1975 concession.
Excludes bonds from present settlement, says no present Chinese action is sought, disclaims espousal and offers actively to discourage attachment of Chinese property.
One presentation point is discretionary; internal explanation cites claimant/Congress compensation and recognition implications as reasons for excluding bonds.

limits: Instruction to make a presentation, not proof of its delivery or the exact October 27 aide-mémoire text.
Retains an irregular subparagraph label 3 where D might be expected and a repeated line in G; no silent emendation.
No evidence that the 1975 retransmission itself changed instructions or that any promised discouragement of litigation occurred.
sources.release_status: Mirror labels current classification UNCLASSIFIED; disposition RELEASED; State systematic-review marking 06 JUL 2006. Historical SECRET/NODIS markings remain in reproduced text.
sources.source_independence: One retransmitted 1973 instruction, not independent 1973 and 1975 policy decisions.

interpretive_boundary: The missing December 22 memorandum, June 14 Chinese note and Solomon attachments remain unrecovered. New evidence clarifies competing positions and American conditions; it neither proves a broken assurance nor identifies the Chinese internal cause of withdrawal.
